city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 68°F was the 2nd warmest November 13 high (tied) of 152 since 1875, the warmest since 1999.
text.p_yest: The high of 68°F was the 2nd warmest November 13 high (tied) of 152 since 1875, the warmest since 1999. The normal high for the date is 50°F, and the record is 69°F (1939). The low of 43°F was the 9th warmest November 13 low (tied) of 150 since 1877.
text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Boise's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Boise has set 10 standing record lows, far fewer than the 66 that chance alone would give, and 105 record highs, far more than the 65 that chance alone would give. The 2020s hold the most record highs of any decade (40). Boise's all-time high is 111°F, on July 12, 1898.
text.t_chg: Boise has warmed, days and nights alike
text.p_chg: Across 147 complete years: Boise's average low has risen +0.20°F per decade (95% range +0.13 to +0.27), about +2.9°F since 1878. Boise's average high has risen +0.15°F per decade (95% range +0.10 to +0.21), about +2.3°F since 1878.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 9 of 12 months. Highs rose in 6 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Boise's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (−0.10 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 11.5 inches a year. The wettest year was 1896 (22.97 in); the driest, 1966 (6.64 in).
